Frequently Asked Questions

At what point does maintaining an old furnace stop making sense compared to replacement?

When documented condition says the next failures are structural rather than component-level. A worn igniter is a repair; a compromised heat exchanger is a replacement conversation with a safety dimension. The inspection states which category the unit occupies and prices the path from there.

Do older Williamston homes have particular electrical risks worth checking?

The recurring ones are ungrounded receptacles, missing GFCI protection near water, and panels loaded past their design era. None is automatically an emergency, but each is worth documenting. An evaluation ranks them so corrections happen in risk order rather than discovery order.

What are the signs my sewer line is failing rather than just clogged?

Frequency and reach. Backups recurring after professional clearing, multiple slow fixtures at once, gurgling at the lowest drains, and unusually green patches over the line’s path all point structural. A camera inspection converts those hints into a documented picture before repair is scoped.

Would an air scrubber help with musty odors in an older home?

It helps with the airborne component, and in-duct treatment works on odors and particles as air cycles. Persistent mustiness also warrants finding the moisture source feeding it, since treatment downstream of an active problem manages symptoms. The visit checks both so the fix is complete.

Which communities near Williamston are in your coverage?

Pelzer, Piedmont, and Easley sit on the same Anderson County routes. The chat team can confirm any address quickly.
